description: E11.1 — Intentional-Defect Corpus manifest. Each fixture is a workbook built in code (packages/core/src/__tests__/defectCorpus.test.ts) carrying a known, planted defect. The test imports each fixture, runs analyzeFindings, and asserts the detector produces findings matching the expected category/severity/minimum count. Constitution §53 rule 7: every detector capability has a fixture that exercises it, and every finding ships with a regression test.

fixtures.name: circular_reference
fixtures.defect: Two cells reference each other (A1=B1+1, B1=A1+1), forming a 2-cell dependency cycle.

fixtures.name: pattern_break
fixtures.defect: In a 7-period column-accumulation row, one cell (E3) references B2 instead of E2, breaking the dominant relative formula shape.

fixtures.name: broken_reference
fixtures.defect: A formula references an empty cell (Z99) that has no content.

fixtures.name: hardcode_in_series
fixtures.defect: A literal number (D3=0.5) embedded in a horizontal run of formula cells, so it will not recalculate when inputs change.

fixtures.name: external_reference
fixtures.defect: A formula pulls from another workbook ([Book2.xlsx]Sheet1!A1), which cannot be resolved deterministically.

fixtures.name: dead_input
fixtures.defect: An input cell (B1=99) is never referenced by any calculation and reaches no output.

fixtures.name: missing_formula
fixtures.defect: A vertical column of formulas has a numeric gap in the middle (B3 literal between B2 and B4 formulas).

fixtures.name: disconnected_output
fixtures.defect: A formula island (C1<->D1 cycle) depends on an input but reaches no terminal output — a dead-end calculation.

notes: Fixtures are generated in-memory via XLSX.utils.aoa_to_sheet + explicit cell assignment, with !ref set to the full used range (required for the parser to see all cells).
The disconnected_output detector only fires on cyclic islands: in an acyclic graph every dead-end formula is itself a terminal, so non-terminal disconnected nodes require a cycle.
external_reference is reported at severity 'warning' by design — external refs are a determinism risk, not a guaranteed error.
